note: EVERY range a control applies, in every app, and the one place to change one (the principal, 2026-11-15). scripts/sync-constants.ts writes it into common/lib/bounds.generated.ts (web), NppsBounds.generated.kt (Compose and Android) and NppsBounds.generated.swift (iOS); `bun scripts/sync-constants.ts --check` fails CI if any is stale or hand-edited. An id is <namespace>.<group>.<field>: `param` is a modality parameter, `limit` a clinician limit, `interval` and `protocol` the timing fields. An edge is { value } or { ref }, where ref names a constant in common/npps/constants.json so a hardware or safety figure still has one copy. basis is natural (cannot be otherwise), hardware (the device or its wire format), practical (what a person can perceive or do), safety (a health or safety limit, with its source) or unestablished (carried over with no source on record: a question for the principal, register row UC-191). A side with no edge is open on purpose and `unbounded` says why. A range bounded on both sides is a slider and any other range is a typed field.

bounds.unbounded: No maximum: the former 100 Hz (40 Hz for deep PBM) is register UC-082, with no derivation. The descriptor carries up to about 4.29 MHz (32-bit millihertz, OI-PBMTILE-01), and the tile refuses a frequency it cannot realise, which the hub sees on read-back. The tile's realisable range is not established (OI-PBMTILE-03), and the cluster controller's design range is 2 to 40 Hz (NP-HW-HUB-001), so no hardware figure is applied yet. The editor step 0.5 is a control step, not a limit.

The documented bound on a beat is the planar path's tone ceiling, carrier plus beat at most 1,000 Hz (REQ-AUDIO-25), which the validator and compiler hold. A binaural beat has a perceptual limit (NP-HW-AUDIO-001 §8.2.7 A), which is not a source for 100.
